triplet: The Babyface, cheering crowd: high-flying moves; cheat, you lose. A slave to approval.
The Heel, cheating: bear hugs, eye pokes. If they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.
The Tweener, Face or Heel on a coin flip: you don't ask for it, so they want you more.
The Jobber, isolated, picked apart; only control: who defeats you.
The Immovable Object, immune to throws: slow gorilla. You Can't Win.
The Aerial Ace dodges any attack; fail, double damage. Stand still, you die.
The Powerhouse Botch off the top rope: crush yourself, or crush everyone.
The Little Giant, surprising strength, lifts the Huge; surprise doubles damage.
The Master Seller, sympathy: reel back, limp to the ring, make them believe.
The No-Sell Monster sits right back up: removes all tension for ego.
The Oversell Clown, reacting far beyond reality: a mockery of the sport. See: Michaels and Hogan.
The Limb Target, called shot: legs, no speed; arms, no lifting. Cruel, logical, effective.
The Thigh Slap didn't hurt, but sounds like it did: an audio lie.
The Stomp Punch, stun with noise: stomping on the mat. Kinetic misdirection.
The Echo Chest: loud noise, but many strikes to actually bruise.
The Chop Fest: nothing but chop, until one quits. A test of endurance.
The Sacred Mask, kayfabe sacred to identity: never remove it.
The Rudo Ripper: instant disqualification, but you win the feud.
The Strong Style Spirit: the more damage you take, the harder you hit back.
The Limp Arm refuses the lockup: sign of a shooter.
The Juice Lover: you can't hurt me if I hurt me first.
The Snake Bag has a live snake: terrify them before the match starts.
The Lazy Genius, hands in pockets: the apathy makes them furious.
The Exotic attacks dignity, not the body: psychological dominance.
The Hot Tag: fresh partner for payback, the explosive release of tension.
The Victim, the Ricky Morton role: isolated and picked apart. You are the bait.
The Wolfpack, brawler, flyer, powerhouse: triple attack on the isolated.
The Savant Manager knows the moves better than they do.
The Pop Hunter: if they want a heel, give them a heel. Want a clown? Honk your nose.
The Empty Arena, pausing for a pop that never comes: silence amplifies impacts.
The Green Screen Crowd pipes in noise: audio sweetening on a lie.
The Plant: I'm just a fan! Gambling on the outcome while part of the show.
The Shooter forces you to sell; refuse, real damage. Stiff the no-seller.
The Sandbag refuses to cooperate: dead weight. Extremely unprofessional.
The Real Injury, unplanned: the crowd goes nuts because it's real.
The Cue Card Holder reveals the next move: short cuts for out-of-depth wrestlers.
The Undead Wizard gets under your skin with smoke and mirrors.
The Uninterested Genius: loaf around, wake up only at critical health.
The Trash Talker, shouting at Michael Cole: hilarious and entertaining abuse.
The Finger Poke of Doom: instant pin if you consent. Strength? No, gullibility.
The Finisher, the Leg Drop, once per match: if this hits, go home.
The False Finish survives the pinfall: the art of the near-fall.
The Squash against any jobber: no-selling, total dominance.
The Time Limit Draw: no winner, both keep dignity. No one loses.
The Booker, before it starts: the ending is pre-planned. You are just a puppet.
The Spot Caller changes the plan mid-match: a basic outline, filled in with sweat.
The Rehearsal, Hogan and Warrior: perfect, but lacks soul.
The Rest Hold: slow down, give the audience a chance to catch up.
The Hard Cam: if the camera didn't see it, it didn't happen.
The Steel Steps, weaponized furniture: environment, not weapon. Usually.
The Ring Post, unforgiving steel: miss a charge, max damage.
The Announcer's Table: shouting at Michael Cole while destroying his desk.
The Internet Smark critiques bad psychology without ever taking a bump.
The Botched Spot, incoherent collection of moves: it just looks messy.
The Kayfabe Police enforce the lie: keep the secrets secret, or get fired.
The Retirement Match: rising, and falling. See you next season.
